title: Jacked Cabbage Man 2.0
author: Trevor N.
desc:
A five day hybrid upper lower split with an emphasis on the chest, shoulders and triceps. Muscle groups get hit at least twice a week. Workouts are 60-70 minutes long and require dumbbells, a barbell, adjustable bench, somewhere to do pull ups and dips, and a cable tower. Access to an EZ curl bar, rings, trap bar, loadable weight vest, and a belt squat machine will be optimal but not mandatory.

Keep things simple yet progressing with the following double progression that you can apply to almost all movements. Use each movement as the warm up, doing 1-3 sets and adding weight until you get to your working sets.

For compound movements, leave one rep in the tank on the first set, then go to near or actual failure (RPE 9.5-10) on the last set(s). For movements where failure is risky or risk to reward is high (RDLs, Squats, ab wheel rollouts, chest flyes), leave a rep in the tank (REP 9).

For isolation or lighter weight movements, go to failure on the first set, then go beyond failure with partial reps if the movement allows or the resistance curve makes sense. For example, a standing overhead cable extension for triceps is hardest at the bottom, so once you hit failure, you can't really do partials. Bayesian curls or preacher curls are another example where partials don't make sense, so I do drop sets instead. Tricep pushdowns, cable lat raises, and rear delt flyes are good examples where you can do partial reps after failure.

ex.note: Warm up to two heavier top sets, then a back-off set at higher reps. 30 degree incline.
Slow down the eccentric, explosive concentric. Do a 1 second engaged pause at the bottom (not a dead hang). Stop when your chin no longer clears the bar. Shoulder width neutral grip or wider.
Alternate having the cable in front or behind you. On the last set, once you can't hit parallel, do 5 more partial reps.
The higher the rings are off the ground, the easier. Work to parallel with the floor, pausing in the deep stretch. Add a weighted vest once you pass 12 reps with body weight.
Wedge shoes/plates/wedge blocks to elevate heels. You should break parallel and get super deep if you have enough heel elevation. Sit in bottom for 1 sec. Use safety squat or BB if no belt squat.

ss.note: Stay partly hinged so the hamstrings are lengthened throughout. Use bands to reduce tension, slowly building tendon and muscle strength. For tracking, BW minus the weight bands are taking away.
Do these kneeling if possible. Breath in at the top stretch to get more stretch, breath out at bottom during contraction. Focus on moving with abs and not hips. Arched spine at top stretch.

ex.note: Warm up to one top heavy set. Pause in the deep stretch 1-2 sec for the first two weighted sets, then go bodyweight for the last set and control the negative but no bottom pause.
Use a barbell, arch bar, or dumbbells. About shoulder width grip. Low incline angle on the bench, 15-30 degrees. After the first 1-2 sets, go past failure with kelso shrugs to hit the upper back.

ss.note: Dumbbells or small plates. Try not to lean too far back as you get close to failure. On the last set, go beyond failure with regular lateral raises.
Experiment with rope and EZ bar attachments, widths, and pull angle to find the sweet spot. Ideally pull to your chin or forehead. Slow eccentric.

ex.note: Low incline, 15-30 degrees. Only come 3/4 of the way up, as there's no tension at the top. Pause in the stretch, push chest to the ceiling, a little locked bend in the elbows (not straight arms).
Stay away from failure, only use this to warm up the posterior chain. No weight needed.

ss.note: Do these on an exercise ball, arching back over the ball to get a nice stretch on the abs. Hold a dumbbell against your upper chest. Only crunch up with your abs, don't come all the way up.

ex.note: Bench set with a 60-75 degree incline. Use a barbell for maximal loading. Push up and back slightly, not forward.
If you prefer using a dumbbell, go for it. I find the EZ bar allows to go heavier and with less strain on hands/wrist. Slight bend to elbows, focus on the stretch. Tuck scapula and focus on lats.

ss.note: Use a arched or cambered barbell and a flat bench so you can go really deep in the stretch. Triceps may be fried, so use a wide grip to really focus on the chest, kind of like a flye.

ex.note: Use a 45 degree incline, one arm at a time, no rest between arms. Go heavier on the first set.

ss.note: Alternate between rope and bar attachments. You can lift a lot more with bar; you can sweep back further with a rope. Each has its place.
Set an incline bench nearly parallel to the floor, chest supported so you can really focus on sweeping your arms out and back. Range of motion will fall throughout, but keep going and don't stop.
